title: Jarring Sichuan-spiced Algerian Sick-day Tagine
description: A pungent and flaky Algerian sick-day dish featuring Sichuan pepper, blanching, and a whole30-friendly twist.

ingredients.name: Ghee
ingredients.notes: clarified butter, high in fat for a rich flavor

ingredients.name: Chicken breast
ingredients.notes: boneless and skinless, dairy-free alternative to traditional lamb or chicken thigh

instructions: Combine Sichuan peppercorns, cumin seeds, and coriander seeds in a small bowl and grind into a coarse spice blend using a mortar and pestle or spice grinder.
Heat ghee in a large salt block over medium heat.
Add the ground spice blend and saut0 the spices for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the sliced ginger and minced garlic and cook for an additional 2 minutes, until the ginger is softened and fragrant.
Add the chopped red onion and cook for 3-4 minutes, until the onion is translucent.
Add the chicken breast and cook for 5-6 minutes, until the chicken is browned on all sides and cooked through.
Add the chopped parsnip and bay leaves to the salt block and cook for an additional 5 minutes, until the parsnip is tender.
Season the tagine with salt and cook for an additional 1 minute, until the flavors have melded together.
Transfer the tagine to a serving dish and serve immediately.
Garnish with fresh herbs, if desired.
Optional: serve with a side of couscous or rice for a more traditional Algerian meal.
